title: Proposed crash damage and repair economics acceptance matrix

baseline.baseline_role: Source identity for this proposed matrix; it is not a test result.

scope.policy: Cases describe target behavior. Existing support, costs, thresholds, fit and physical validity must be established during execution; this document asserts no passing result.
scope.profile_selection: Profile labels are proposed fixture selectors, not existing schema identifiers. Resolve them from installed aircraft capabilities and authored configurations at test execution; do not interpret an empty selector as a pass.

priorities.P0: Release-blocking for an in-scope supported feature or an explicitly disclosed unsupported boundary.
priorities.P1: Required focused extension or comparison; schedule and qualification must be explicit.

scope.status_meaning: proposed_not_executed means no execution, pass, failure or validation is claimed.

case_schema.applicable_profiles: Fixture selectors resolved against installed capabilities.

cases.setup: Replay a controlled fast, shallow touchdown within the aircraft landing envelope: low sink, little lateral slip, aligned wheels, no propeller or hull contact, and no overload indicated by the accepted contact evidence.
cases.expected_damage: No gear damage solely because forward speed is high; retain healthy gear when the authored ground-load policy finds no damaging load.
cases.expected_economics: No repair purchase or false accident total for this landing; a normal landing does not become an aircraft write-off.
invariants: Groundspeed alone is not a damage threshold.
The same accepted evidence gives the same result at every render cadence.

cases.setup: Compare a controlled normal landing with a hard-sink landing, holding aircraft, surface, forward speed and attitude as close as the fixture permits; author the hard case to cross the reviewed gear-damage policy.
cases.expected_damage: The hard case resolves the affected gear or mount according to its declared load and construction, with any unrelated zones retained as unaffected.
cases.expected_economics: Price only the selected gear and mount actions; keep missing component prices explicitly unknown.
invariants: Do not substitute the aircraft purchase price for the gear price.
No validated numeric load threshold is implied by this fixture.

cases.setup: Replay aligned and substantial lateral-slip landings at similar vertical sink and forward speed; use accepted side-load or a documented game proxy where the physical signal is unavailable.
cases.expected_damage: The side-load case assesses the loaded leg and mount under the lateral damage policy; the aligned case remains governed by its own evidence.
cases.expected_economics: The cost follows the affected gear, any documented mount repair, and their compatible prices; unknown side-load costs stay explicitly estimated or unresolved.
invariants: Lateral and normal channels remain distinguishable.
The policy does not claim measured gear failure strength.

cases.setup: Touch down on one main leg with the opposite leg clear, then stop without a further impact; repeat mirrored with equivalent conditions.
cases.expected_damage: Resolve only the contacted leg and its authored load-path neighbors, with left and right swapped in the mirrored run.
cases.expected_economics: Price only the affected side, respecting whether the actual part is sold singly or as a pair.
invariants: Avoid duplicate pair purchases and false damage on the other side.
Receipt and presentation identify the impacted side when the profile supports it.

cases.setup: Use equivalent hard landings for a fixed-gear profile and a retract profile with the gear down; select reviewed per-profile leg, attachment, actuator and package policies.
cases.expected_damage: Assess the loaded leg and mount separately; consider retract mechanism damage only where installed and supported by the event and authored policy.
cases.expected_economics: Use each aircraft’s compatible repair or package costs rather than a generic percentage of aircraft price.
invariants: Fixed and retract hardware remain distinct.
An absent or unpriced retract mechanism is not assigned zero cost.

cases.setup: Compare a wheels-up runway landing with the intended supported belly landing of a gearless aircraft, using each model’s explicit contact role and comparable impact severity.
cases.expected_damage: The retracted-gear scenario assesses the contacted belly and exposed structure; the intended supported landing is not automatically classified as gear failure.
cases.expected_economics: Charge only selected local repair actions and any documented downstream parts; no imaginary landing-gear purchase for a gearless aircraft.
invariants: Contact role and aircraft configuration are explicit.
Identical visual poses do not force identical hardware assumptions.

cases.setup: Replay a wingtip brush with low normal and tangential contact exposure, intact covering by the reviewed gameplay policy, and no secondary contact.
cases.expected_damage: The contacted zone remains intact or inspection-only under the declared policy; no damaged spar or opposite-wing disposition is invented.
cases.expected_economics: Allow zero material repair when inspection is resolved and free under the fixture policy; otherwise label any inspection amount or missing fee explicitly.
invariants: Normal contact severity and location are recorded.
A zero charge requires an explicit supported decision.

cases.setup: Inject or reproduce a covering-only tear with an inspected intact spar and a compatible local patch recipe.
cases.expected_damage: Resolve covering damage without declaring spar or entire wing replacement.
cases.expected_economics: Price the selected compatible patch and chosen labor and material basis; distinguish consumed material from package purchase.
invariants: A structural damage flag cannot be hidden by a covering-only recipe.
Do not double count a purchased package and its consumed fraction.

cases.setup: Create a medium wingtip impact that crosses the reviewed local-repair tier but does not implicate the root, opposite wing or onboard electronics.
cases.expected_damage: Mark the contacted wing zone repairable and leave unrelated components unchanged unless a declared load path independently affects them.
cases.expected_economics: Use a compatible local repair estimate and scoped prices; do not replace the full aircraft merely because the flight stops.
invariants: Outcome is derived from a declared game policy, not claimed measured failure data.
Unknown price remains unknown.

cases.setup: Create a much more severe direct wing-root or fuselage impact under a reviewed catastrophic tier, and define which components have separately supported survival evidence.
cases.expected_damage: Resolve the documented structural losses and only their authored downstream effects; let an explicit total-loss policy decide whether whole-build replacement is the economic alternative.
cases.expected_economics: Compute affected replacement or repair versus a compatible whole-build alternative, deducting supported reuse exactly once.
invariants: Terminal flight and economic total loss are separate decisions.
Do not invent survival or damage for unobserved components.

cases.setup: Replay equivalent left and right wing contacts on an aircraft with separately mapped halves and repair parts.
cases.expected_damage: The same local outcome follows the mirrored contacted side; the opposite wing and its controls are unchanged absent additional evidence.
cases.expected_economics: Price the relevant side or a correctly documented shared wing package without a second purchase.
invariants: Geometry, part identity and price coverage use the same side.
Aggregate-only dossiers must say localization is unavailable.

cases.setup: Compare equal total-speed direct and glancing contacts against the same target and surface, using matched local geometry and distinct normal and tangential components.
cases.expected_damage: The normal-impact and abrasion channels differ according to their declared policies; glancing contact is not forced to match a direct impact.
cases.expected_economics: Each cost follows its own local outcome and compatible repair, without speed-times-aircraft-price formulas.
invariants: No universal speed-only crash or survival rule.
No double counting of a shared simultaneous energy budget.

cases.setup: Reproduce a nonterminal powered propeller strike with a positive disc contact and an accepted strike event; keep surrounding structure clear.
cases.expected_damage: Resolve the struck propeller once and assess relevant shaft, mount and engine or motor separately; do not automatically destroy the engine.
cases.expected_economics: Price one compatible propeller replacement plus any explicitly selected inspection or repair; absent prices remain unknown.
invariants: One physical part is not purchased twice.
Unrelated spinner and engine are not automatically billed.

cases.setup: Compare a stopped propeller physically struck by the ground with a stopped propeller that remains clear; include a powered strike as a separate condition.
cases.expected_damage: A documented unpowered blade contact is assessed according to its impact evidence, while a clear disc creates no blade damage; powered contact retains its own policy.
cases.expected_economics: Price only the resulting blade and independently supported powertrain actions.
invariants: Do not infer a strike from RPM alone.
Unpowered does not automatically mean undamaged.

cases.setup: Construct one accepted tick with a terminal nose or gear collision and a separately evidenced intersecting propeller disc.
cases.expected_damage: Retain both the terminal contact and propeller evidence; classify the blade once without inventing unobserved engine damage.
cases.expected_economics: The propeller appears once in the incident estimate if the model establishes damage; any other components follow their own evidence.
invariants: Same-tick event ordering cannot erase propeller evidence.
Duplicate publication cannot duplicate a purchase.

cases.setup: Sweep a propeller or blade through a scenery obstacle while fuselage probes remain clear, and run a matched clear-disc control.
cases.expected_damage: A supported propeller-obstacle contact yields a documented localized outcome; the clear-disc control has no invented blade contact.
cases.expected_economics: Apply compatible propeller and independently supported powertrain prices, with explicit unknowns if the obstacle geometry cannot determine a contact.
invariants: Do not relabel a hull-only collision as a proven propeller hit.
Unavailable disc detection stays explicit until implemented.

cases.setup: Impact a wing or tail while the propeller, nose, motor and engine remain clear and there is no fire or water exposure.
cases.expected_damage: Leave the powertrain and propeller unaffected or explicitly unresolved according to installation evidence; do not assign damage from overall crash severity alone.
cases.expected_economics: No automatic propeller or engine replacement line; preserve eligible reusable components without double credit.
invariants: A terminal flight is not proof that every installed component was destroyed.
Price attribution follows contact and load paths.

cases.setup: Compare a local nose or mount strike with an airframe-loss scenario in which the engine or motor and receiver are separately outside the affected zones and have no hazard exposure.
cases.expected_damage: For the nose strike, inspect or damage the specific mount and powertrain components based on evidence; for the distant airframe loss, apply the declared reusable-component policy.
cases.expected_economics: Deduct supported reused engine or motor and receiver once from the replacement alternative; do not deduct damaged or unknown parts as if confirmed reusable.
invariants: Receiver, engine or motor, mount and propeller have independent dispositions.
No salvage credit exists without a compatible physical inventory binding.

cases.setup: Compare a mild isolated wing or gear incident with a direct high-energy turbine-installation strike using the reviewed turbine profile, at matched instrumentation and explicit geometry.
cases.expected_damage: The mild local case leaves the turbine outside the damage path when evidence supports that conclusion; the direct case receives the authored turbine and mount assessment or remains unresolved if evidence is insufficient.
cases.expected_economics: Preserve the turbine when its reuse is supported; price repair or replacement only for supported damage, and expose any unpriced component.
invariants: No universal speed guarantees turbine survival or destruction.
No propeller part is invented for a turbine.

cases.setup: Create an accepted local battery-pack impact that meets the reviewed damaged-pack rule but has no modeled ignition or thermal runaway.
cases.expected_damage: Replace the damaged pack under the declared policy; keep unrelated parts separate and do not invent a fire.
cases.expected_economics: Include one compatible pack replacement and independently supported local repairs, with unknown prices explicitly marked.
invariants: Pack damage does not require visible flame.
No VFX condition determines damage.

cases.setup: Replay the same initial damaged pack with and without a separately evidenced delayed thermal event after flight motion has stopped.
cases.expected_damage: Both runs retain the initial pack damage; only the confirmed thermal event can add affected nearby components or revoke their provisional reuse.
cases.expected_economics: Bill each damaged unit once and update only additional evidenced losses; retain any unknown price or hazard condition.
invariants: The delayed event has deterministic timing and an idempotent identity.
No thermal bill is inferred solely from cinematic fire.

cases.setup: Generate a valid lake event whose probe_source is propeller and whose probe_id resolves to the installed propeller; keep an equivalent non-propeller lake event as control.
cases.expected_damage: Retain water exposure and map the qualified propeller probe to the proper local component; do not claim physical blade breakage without a separate disposition rule.
cases.expected_economics: Show relevant affected or inspected part identities and any separately evidenced repair; unresolved water and powertrain costs remain explicit.
invariants: Source-qualified probe mapping is used.
The event is not silently reduced to only a generic structural note.

cases.setup: Compare a water entry with an otherwise comparable bank-ground collision, including recoverable and unretrieved variants where authored.
cases.expected_damage: Water exposure affects the relevant electronics and powertrain assessment; bank-only contact does not invent water exposure. Retrieval is explicit.
cases.expected_economics: Apply retrieval, replacement and salvage rules only to supported facts; no automatic zero for missing electronics costs.
invariants: Material identity and retrieval are retained across checkpoint and report.
No blanket aircraft write-off from a bank-only hit.

cases.setup: Compare fuel leakage without an ignition source, a supported ignition event, and a water or wet environment, using declared energy and thermal evidence.
cases.expected_damage: Leaking fuel alone is not fire; only an explicit physical or game-policy ignition event can create thermal damage, including potential low-visibility combustion.
cases.expected_economics: Charge evidenced thermal losses and inspections only; an unresolved ignition or damage state remains labeled.
invariants: An explosion or flame effect is neither required nor sufficient evidence.
No aircraft-wide or fixed-speed-only ignition rule.

cases.setup: Replay the identical incident with effects on and off, camera near and far, and with optional secondary visual simulation skipped; run the deterministic gameplay aftermath and settlement to completion.
cases.expected_damage: The same committed component damage and explicitly modeled aftermath result in each run, independently of visual debris, fire, frame rate or camera.
cases.expected_economics: Compare identical dispositions, amounts, range, provenance and settlement timing after excluding only explicitly nondeterministic presentation metadata.
invariants: Secondary visual impacts cannot create extra damage or charges.
A deterministic gameplay secondary contact is recorded independently of visual simulation.

cases.setup: Start a low-severity hull contact, maintain the same contact episode while severity or scrape exposure increases, then separate.
cases.expected_damage: The bounded episode summary retains the onset, relevant peak or accumulated quantity, final disposition and affected zone, including escalation when the declared policy calls for it.
cases.expected_economics: Recalculate one action per affected unit without missing later escalation or repeatedly purchasing a part.
invariants: Persistent ticks are not ignored as damage evidence.
Continuous contact does not produce a purchase per frame.

cases.setup: Deliver the same accepted event and same inspection receipt repeatedly before and after report publication, including exact duplicate and same-ID conflicting payload variants.
cases.expected_damage: Exact repeats do not change damage; a conflicting same-ID receipt is rejected without mutation.
cases.expected_economics: No duplicate cost, salvage credit, revision or history entry.
invariants: Identities are stable and bounded.
The rejected conflict leaves the report unchanged.

cases.setup: Force a candidate contact tick to fail solver or transaction admission, then retry an accepted tick from the previous state.
cases.expected_damage: Rejected candidate evidence cannot modify damage, visual state, committed episode history or checkpoint.
cases.expected_economics: No report revision, archive write, cost or salvage arises from the rejected candidate.
invariants: A later accepted event can still be processed once.
Physics and economic state remain transactionally paired.

cases.setup: Submit independent simultaneous contacts in all deterministic input orderings and replay a multi-contact episode with the same accepted total exposure.
cases.expected_damage: Equivalent permutations produce the same per-zone dispositions and bounded exposure assignment.
cases.expected_economics: The same parts and totals result without overlap or duplicated energy-related claims.
invariants: Sort or otherwise canonicalize unordered input.
Never allocate more than the declared shared episode budget.

cases.setup: Exceed the current 128-event diagnostic journal with accepted contacts, then introduce a new wing or gear zone contact, a prop strike and water exposure.
cases.expected_damage: Bounded per-zone summaries retain late relevant facts or explicitly identify overflow and missing scope; prop and water facts are not lost.
cases.expected_economics: Later billable evidence is not silently omitted or double charged; any unbounded uncertainty remains explicit.
invariants: Memory and checkpoint sizes remain bounded.
A generic overflow warning does not pretend to reconstruct missing local damage.

cases.setup: Confirm a component reusable through a valid assessment, then deliver a later accepted impact to that same component and a separate contact to another component.
cases.expected_damage: New local evidence reopens the affected reusable disposition; unrelated reuse remains intact, and the earlier receipt remains an immutable historical record.
cases.expected_economics: Recompute only affected salvage and repairs; never retain stale reuse as a confirmed current credit.
invariants: Compare evidence chronology, not only component ID.
A repeated copy of the same later event is idempotent.

cases.setup: Confirm an engine, motor or mount replacement, then submit a later propeller strike that requests inspection of the same component.
cases.expected_damage: The already confirmed replacement is not downgraded to mere inspection; previously reusable adjacent components may be reopened only where new evidence applies.
cases.expected_economics: The confirmed replacement cost is retained once along with any new propeller cost.
invariants: Damage state is monotone absent an explicit completed repair transaction.
Receipt provenance survives recalculation.

cases.setup: Save a paired active-flight checkpoint after a localized impact and partial assessment, restore it in a compatible session, and continue with the same accepted inputs.
cases.expected_damage: The restored incident, component state, per-zone evidence, deduplication IDs and settlement continue consistently with the uninterrupted run.
cases.expected_economics: Compare frozen prices, repair decisions, credit, report and subsequent revisions; duplicate receipts remain idempotent.
invariants: Reject incompatible physics, price, recipe or contact bindings before mutating either half.
Terminal reports remain view-only until a supported terminal-resume contract exists.

cases.setup: Restore an unpaired physics-only checkpoint made after a prior hull brush ended, with no active contact and no latched propeller strike.
cases.expected_damage: Earlier damage history is explicitly unavailable rather than implicitly clean; no fabricated contact or physical damage is added.
cases.expected_economics: The report clearly distinguishes unknown history from zero loss, or an equivalent persistent restore warning is presented.
invariants: Compare with an active-contact and latched-propeller legacy restore.
Do not silently transfer the previous live ledger to an unrelated checkpoint.

cases.setup: Replay one fixed accepted input tape under 30, 60 and 144 Hz render publication, including a sustained contact, duplicate event, aftermath and stable-ground settlement.
cases.expected_damage: Identical accepted physical events and component dispositions occur; the same deterministic tick triggers settlement.
cases.expected_economics: Reports match in amounts, affected units, provenance, evidence and completeness after excluding only documented identity or wall-clock metadata.
invariants: Report evaluation and disk writes occur outside accepted physics callbacks.
Software determinism is not physical validation.

cases.setup: Resolve every affected component for a local accident using an aircraft whose unrelated inventory remains unpriced; run a second case with one affected price missing.
cases.expected_damage: Unaffected components are explicitly assessed outside the incident scope, while any genuinely uncertain component remains unresolved.
cases.expected_economics: Permit a complete scoped repair total only when all required incident costs and decisions are resolved; keep complete-build replacement completeness and affected missing prices separate.
invariants: Do not hide unassessed damage to narrow the range.
Do not represent an unavailable amount as zero.

cases.setup: Enumerate every airplane route from the actual current catalog, including player-selectable and retained nonselectable variants, then exercise its source identity, contact mappings and a relevant damage-to-report fixture.
cases.expected_damage: Each route either produces a supported local component assessment or an explicit incomplete condition; no vehicle silently inherits an unrelated profile.
cases.expected_economics: Every required affected component has a compatible price, documented proxy or visible unknown; package scope and whole-build completeness are checked separately.
invariants: Use discovery at execution time rather than assuming the baseline route count.
Treat the historical Skywalker X8 alias as the current canonical route, not an extra aircraft.

cases.setup: Enumerate the X-Cell research route and any future rotorcraft separately; inspect its own contact, installed inventory and economic identity contracts.
cases.expected_damage: Do not claim a helicopter crash model from fixed-wing gear or propeller fixtures; unsupported rotor, skid and drivetrain cases remain explicitly unavailable.
cases.expected_economics: Do not issue an airplane-based bill or use the HX-700 visual surrogate as proof of X-Cell parts; record missing BOM and prices until the rotorcraft gate is met.
invariants: Helicopter acceptance is independent from the airplane release gate.
A visual model does not establish a physical inventory.

cases.setup: Exercise stock aircraft sourceRef resolution, a documented registered battery or propulsion variant, a harmless text-only edit, and a change to an economically relevant part or contact binding.
cases.expected_damage: Retain compatible model bindings for an allowed sourceRef or registered variant; reject or explicitly mark stale an economically relevant identity mismatch.
cases.expected_economics: Use the correct variant-specific price and frozen provenance; do not attach an incompatible propeller, battery or dossier.
invariants: Fingerprint includes all fields affecting damage, installation, contact-to-part mapping and valuation, with schema version.
An allowed text-only change cannot silently rebind changed physical inventory.

cases.setup: Load a newly authored aircraft with a documented, approved class fallback and then a version with a missing or incompatible class mapping.
cases.expected_damage: The approved class profile produces bounded, explicitly identified game-policy dispositions; missing required mapping is reported as unavailable instead of silently using another aircraft’s profile.
cases.expected_economics: Compatible class-level cost proxies carry their source, scope and estimate label; absent prices or package compatibility stay unknown.
invariants: A fallback is explicit, versioned and overridable by a compatible aircraft-specific profile.
No fabricated exact bill or physical qualification claim.

cases.setup: Quote repairs needing a subset of parts from a multi-item package, a pair package, and overlapping whole-airframe plus subassembly alternatives using fixture prices and quantities.
cases.expected_damage: Each required affected physical unit is covered by a compatible option; unused surplus is recorded without inventing extra damage.
cases.expected_economics: Compare valid coverage options once, avoid purchasing the same unit twice, and distinguish package cash outlay from material consumption.
invariants: Do not add a kit and already included parts as separate purchases.
Unknown compatibility or price prevents a false optimal claim.

cases.setup: Compare a local repair with a compatible whole-build replacement after an inspection or retrieval fee has already been incurred; include DIY and paid-labor selections.
cases.expected_damage: Repair choices follow compatible damage classes and an explicit decision to repair or replace.
cases.expected_economics: Include already incurred fees in both alternatives where applicable and distinguish scoped repair, total incident cost and replacement comparison; label taxes, shipping and excluded costs.
invariants: A whole-build price is not called an unconditional upper bound when incurred fees or excluded costs sit outside it.
No labor charge is counted twice.

cases.setup: Freeze an incident and its catalog, then refresh a seller price, remove an offer or mark a documented proxy stale while opening the prior incident.
cases.expected_damage: No physical damage state changes solely due to a price refresh.
cases.expected_economics: The archived report retains its original dated values and source; any re-quote is separate, versioned and explicitly identifies missing or changed prices.
invariants: No network or disk price lookup occurs inside a physics tick.
Unknown or unavailable prices are not silently replaced with zero.

release_gates.name: Catalog and identity coverage
release_gates.evidence_required: Discover all current airplane routes and variants from the authoritative catalog; prove compatible sourceRef, fingerprint, inventory, contact-zone and price or visible-unknown coverage. List each route and unresolved gap.

release_gates.name: Local damage and gear behavior
release_gates.evidence_required: Execute the landing and local-structure cases for representative fixed, retractable, gearless, balsa and foam profiles, including sides, hard sink, side-load and glancing controls.

release_gates.name: Powertrain and hazards
release_gates.evidence_required: Execute powered and stopped propeller, same-tick terminal, object, engine and receiver salvage, turbine, pack, water and conditional fire cases; record unsupported conditions.

release_gates.name: Financial arithmetic and disclosure
release_gates.evidence_required: Prove incident-scope completeness, compatible package coverage, net salvage once, labor and already-incurred fees, documented range basis, price provenance and unknown-price handling.

release_gates.name: Accepted-event integrity and persistence
release_gates.evidence_required: Prove duplicate, rejected tick, event ordering, long scrape, overflow, later evidence and paired or unpaired checkpoint behavior with bounded state and no double charge.

release_gates.name: Determinism and gameplay presentation
release_gates.evidence_required: Replay accepted tapes across publication cadences, effects and camera settings; compare component assessment, financial results, settlement and the rendered representation against the same gameplay facts.

release_gates.name: Full application and player acceptance
release_gates.evidence_required: Exercise actual launch, flight, report, settlement, restart and restoration on the supported target application and host; inspect readable UI and rendered damage with representative aircraft, report build and environment identity.

release_gates.name: Independent modeling and rotorcraft boundary
release_gates.evidence_required: Review profile calibration against independent construction, repair and expert evidence; separately qualify rotorcraft inventory and collision contracts or state explicitly that rotorcraft damage economics is unavailable.

validation_boundaries.software: Unit and integration fixtures establish implementation behavior only for their recorded source, inputs and environment; they do not prove realistic damage or exact cross-platform physics.
validation_boundaries.full_application_and_browser: A real application run must use the actual production launch and incident/report flow. Browser interaction is relevant only if a browser-hosted production route exists; native Godot evidence does not become browser evidence by assertion. Record host, build, settings and observed interaction.
validation_boundaries.physical: Numerical determinism, screenshots, expert agreement and matching fitted examples do not establish physical validation. Use independent component or repair evidence, holdout cases and documented uncertainty. No crash-testing of a real aircraft is a prerequisite.
validation_boundaries.performance: Measure bounded episode tracking, report generation, persistence and presentation on the accepted target host; source inspection and unrelated benchmarks cannot establish target frame or physics budgets.
